name: Cheekcowl
description: The hatchet is held upright before the face with the free hand behind it, covering the throat from a high strike.

name: Bitblow
description: The wrist snaps the head down in a short arc, landing the bit on the opponent's collarbone.

name: Kerfblow
description: With the elbow tucked in, the hatchet sweeps flat at waist height and bites into the opponent's flank.

name: Fouling Chock
description: The blunt back of the head raps the knuckles of a weapon hand, jarring the grip loose.

name: Angled Helve
description: The helve tilts across the line of an incoming cut so that the blade skids off to the side.

name: Toehop
description: Weight rolls onto the rear hip and one foot slides back, carrying the body out of reach after a swing.

name: Hard Billet
description: Each stroke lands in the same notch, as on a cordwood billet, so the edge goes exactly where it is aimed.

name: Kerfdash
description: Short wrist-only chops, repeated three times in a breath, land fast cuts along a limb as along a stick of kindling.

name: Planted Poll
description: Feet planted like a woodcutter at the billet, knees soft, the hatchet held crosswise to take a shove.

name: Beardhusk
description: The beard of the head catches a sleeve or wrist and tugs sharply, spoiling the opponent's balance.

name: Light Fell
description: Short sliding steps, as along the side of a woodpile, carry the user sideways with the hatchet arm kept free.

name: Chockdrop
description: The arm rises beside the ear and the hatchet falls straight, the shoulder and not the wrist giving the weight.

name: Upward Axehew
description: From a low hang, the hatchet whips up and across with the back of the hand leading, catching the opponent's ribs.

name: Bitbump
description: With the elbow pinned to the side, a tight chop lands inside the opponent's reach before they can answer.

name: Catching Beard
description: The free hand seizes the opponent's wrist while the hatchet hooks behind the elbow, pinning the arm for a moment.

name: Raised Cheek
description: The hatchet sweeps across the chest in a flat arc and slaps a thrust or cut away to the outside.

name: Solid Eye
description: A wide low stance with the hatchet hanging across the thigh lets the user take a push without losing footing.

name: Heeldodge
description: A quick skipping step carries the user forward past the opponent's lead foot and into striking range.

name: Narrow Billet
description: The hatchet leaves the belt loop in an upward arc that runs straight into a cut at the opponent's forearm.

name: Fellhit
description: With a pack still on the shoulders, a short horizontal swing keeps the body balanced while the head bites the leading arm.

name: Leaden Poll
description: The bit drags along a held haft or strap, parting grips and cords with a pulling cut.

name: Hitching Helve
description: A short elbow shove with the flat of the head checks an opponent who steps in too close.

name: Tight Haftswell
description: The hatchet covers the head while the pack takes the blow across the back, turning a clumsy attacker aside.

name: Skipping Kerf
description: Stepping back with the free hand raised, the user opens distance and keeps the hatchet hand cocked.

name: Descending Chock
description: A rolling wrist turn flicks the head around in a tight circle and lands a snapping cut.

name: Straight Handlenub
description: The hand slides down to the helve's end, lengthening the arc so the bit lands a step farther than expected.

name: Eyedash
description: Gripping close under the head, the user chops in a cramped space where a longer swing would foul.

name: Firm Fell
description: The forearm whips the hatchet out in a flat line, striking the guard arm hard enough to numb it.

name: Snug Handlenub
description: With the thumb braced on the flat, the hatchet is held steady before the chest against repeated cuts.

name: Pulling Toe
description: The helve traps an incoming wrist against the hatchet's head and a twist locks the hand in place.

name: Cheekpace
description: A springing half step from the balls of the feet slips the body off the line of a cut.

name: Pushing Kerf
description: Reversed in the grip, the beard hooks the opponent's belt or sleeve and yanks, pulling their posture off balance.

name: Cheekhit
description: A thin thread of qi runs down the arm into the head as it falls, making the plain chop bite deeper.

name: Ready Beard
description: Slow breath carries qi into the forearm while the hatchet is held up, hardening the guard against cuts.

name: Turning Poll
description: A pulse of qi through the poll jars the opponent's weapon hand harder than the blow alone.

name: Stepping Billet
description: Qi in the legs lightens a single sidestep that clears the line of an incoming thrust.

name: Single Axehew
description: Drawn from the belt, the hatchet wakes with a thread of qi along its edge and cuts as it comes up.

name: Kept Heel
description: The short helve is held across the body in both hands, absorbing a descending cut on the wood.

name: Settled Poll
description: The head of the hatchet swings out to meet a blade and turns it past the user's shoulder.

name: Resting Bit
description: The beard catches a thrusting blade and a short pull drags it off its line.

name: Toe Cowl
description: Qi gathered at the forearm lets it take a glancing blow while the hatchet stays ready to answer.

name: Downward Helve
description: Right after the parry, the wrist rolls over and the bit falls on the opponent's exposed hand.

name: Backward Eye
description: Stepping back with the hatchet held high keeps the guard in place while the gap opens.

name: Beardstrike
description: A wide sweeping cut, like clearing a path through bramble, rakes the opponent's guard arm with qi in the wrist.

name: Towing Handlenub
description: The beard hooks a trailing sleeve or strap and pulls it taut, dragging the opponent half a step off balance.

name: Chockbump
description: A rising backhand slices across the opponent's wrist as it would through a thick green stem.

name: Blunt Splinter
description: A low cut at the level of the ankles bites through hose and boot, with qi gathered at the edge.

name: Hooding Bit
description: Held low across the shins, the hatchet turns away a kick or low blow the way it would a branch.

name: Billetwedge
description: The shoulder drives in behind the hatchet's flat, shoving a blocking arm aside to open a lane.

name: Sideways Axehew
description: Backing out along the cleared path in two measured steps, the user keeps the hatchet between self and foe.

name: Fell Drop
description: A short chop thrown from a half-extended elbow lands on the shoulder of an opponent who has closed in.

name: Nabbing Cheek
description: An elbow drives into the clinch, with the hatchet's flat against the opponent's ribs, and forces the bodies apart.

name: Eyestay
description: The beard hooks behind a knee or elbow in a tight space and drags the limb out of position.

name: Lowered Beard
description: The hatchet is tucked tight against the chest with elbows in, leaving no gap for a close thrust.

name: Swaying Toe
description: On the ball of one foot the user turns half around in the press, leaving the opponent's line empty.

name: Billetdrop
description: A flick of the wrist alone snaps the head sideways across the opponent's hand at a hand's breadth.

name: Wide Haftswell
description: The beard catches the opponent's guard and lifts it, and the bit falls in the same stroke.

name: Axehew Bump
description: After the chop lands, the hatchet is drawn back with the beard dragging along the wound.

name: Tripping Axehew
description: The beard snags the back of the opponent's knee and pulls, buckling the leg.

name: Helvestay
description: Hooking the wrist, the user draws the opponent's arm across their own body and holds it there.

name: Chockstrike
description: Two chops fall on one spot in quick succession, the second landing as the first is parried.

name: Heel Wedge
description: The beard catches the crossguard of an incoming blade and wrenches it aside.

name: Holding Heel
description: With the beard turned outward and the arm braced, the hatchet makes a standing screen against slashes.

name: Nimble Poll
description: As the hook pulls the opponent's arm, the user steps in along the same line.

name: Low Handlenub
description: A straight overhead fall of the head onto the opponent's shoulder or raised arm.

name: Eyehit
description: A level cut from the hip crosses the opponent's body at waist height with a thread of qi.

name: Solid Cheek
description: The helve is held before the body at a slant, giving cover against cuts from above.

name: Stopping Billet
description: The back of the head shoves into the opponent's chest and stops their advance for a breath.

name: Beardtrot
description: One foot slides out to the flank and the other follows, bringing the user off the opponent's line.
